method: Direct source inspection of jft-design-system.css, jft-responsive.css, homepage.css, trade-regions.css, header.html, footer.html; exhaustive grep for .hero-btns and .prod-img/.prod-card across the full site; direct image analysis of all 84 product source images via Pillow (actual pixel dimensions vs. declared HTML width/height); direct visual inspection of 2 sample product photos.

design_system_inventory.card_radius_classification: MINOR INCONSISTENCY - not fixed, defensible intentional differentiation
design_system_inventory.section_padding_classification: MINOR INCONSISTENCY - not fixed, no visible harm

findings.title: Regional-page primary hero CTA is invisible on all 4 pages
findings.evidence: trade-regions.css line ~78-80: .hero-btns { display: none !important; }. All 4 regional pages (africa-trade.html, asia-trade.html, europe-trade.html, uae-trade.html) load trade-regions.css and each has its own inline .hero-btns{display:flex} rule with no !important, so the external rule wins unconditionally.
findings.impact: the single highest-value above-the-fold CTA on 4 market-landing pages renders as if it does not exist
findings.root_cause: trade-regions.css is a shared override file reused across category and regional templates; the .hero-btns rule appears to be leftover from a different context and was never checked against the regional-page hero, which needs it visible
findings.fix: remove/neutralize the display:none !important rule in trade-regions.css

findings.title: Category-page product-card images render distorted (stretched/squished)
findings.evidence: measured all 84 product source images with Pillow: 68/84 (81%) are not square, 45/84 (54%) have a ratio outside 0.75-1.3 (as extreme as 0.58:1 and 2.72:1). scripts/build_category_pages.py declares every card image as width=1024 height=1024 (square) regardless of actual file dimensions. No stylesheet (jft-design-system.css, jft-responsive.css, trade-regions.css) sets object-fit or aspect-ratio on .prod-img/.prod-img img. jft-responsive.css has an object-fit:cover rule but it targets the differently-named .product-img (singular) class, confirmed not to apply here.
findings.affected_pages: all 10 Phase 10 category pages, roughly 68 of 84 product cards across them
findings.impact: directly undermines the 'professional commodity catalogue' perception that Phase 10's category architecture was built to create
findings.root_cause: the Phase 10 category-page generator never gave .prod-img a fixed-ratio container, and no shared stylesheet filled the gap
findings.fix: add .prod-img { aspect-ratio: 1/1; overflow: hidden; } and .prod-img img { width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:cover; } to trade-regions.css

findings.title: Amateur/inconsistent product photography style
findings.evidence: direct visual inspection of 2 sample images shows informal hand-held trade/QA-style photography rather than styled product photography, combined with the 81% non-square measurement above
findings.reason_not_fixed: Phase 12 requires documenting CURRENT/PROBLEM/REPLACEMENT-REQUIREMENT/WHY for any image replacement and explicitly prohibits fabricating/sourcing imagery without proper rights; this session cannot commission or verify real JFT Agro product photography. Finding 2's fix improves presentation of the existing photos without needing new photography.

findings_not_actioned.reason: defensible intentional differentiation (structured catalogue vs. soft trust cards), not a clear defect; normalizing without harm-evidence would be an arbitrary stylistic change

findings_not_actioned.topic: category-page section padding vs sitewide token
